author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: فَإِذَا ٱنسَلَخَ ٱلْأَشْهُرُ ٱلْحُرُمُ فَٱقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ وَخُذُوهُمْ وَٱحْصُرُوهُمْ وَٱقْعُدُوا۟ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ ۚ فَإِن تَابُوا۟ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَوُا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ فَخَلُّوا۟ سَبِيلَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/9:5)
english: And when the inviolable months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they should repent, establish prayer, and give zakāh, let them [go] on their way. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 187
what_it_says: After the sacred months end, believers are to kill the polytheists wherever they find them, capture, besiege and ambush them, and release them only if they repent, pray and pay zakat.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: قَـٰتِلُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلَا بِٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِ وَلَا يُحَرِّمُونَ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَلَا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ ٱلْحَقِّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ حَتَّىٰ يُعْطُوا۟ ٱلْجِزْيَةَ عَن يَدٍ وَهُمْ صَـٰغِرُونَ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/9:29)
english: Fight against those who do not believe in Allāh or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allāh and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth [i.e., Islām] from those who were given the Scripture - [fight] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 191
what_it_says: Fight those of the People of the Book who do not hold the religion of truth until they pay the jizya while humbled.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ قَـٰتِلُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْكُفَّارِ وَلْيَجِدُوا۟ فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً ۚ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/9:123)
english: O you who have believed, fight against those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allāh is with the righteous.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 207
what_it_says: Believers are told to fight the disbelievers nearest to them and let those disbelievers find harshness in them.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ جَـٰهِدِ ٱلْكُفَّارَ وَٱلْمُنَـٰفِقِينَ وَٱغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ وَمَأْوَىٰهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/9:73)
english: O Prophet, fight against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 199
what_it_says: The Prophet is told to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and to be harsh with them.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: وَقَـٰتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ ٱلدِّينُ كُلُّهُۥ لِلَّهِ ۚ فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوْا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/8:39)
english: And fight against them until there is no fitnah and [until] the religion [i.e., worship], all of it, is for Allāh. And if they cease - then indeed, Allāh is Seeing of what they do.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 181
what_it_says: Believers are told to fight until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for God; if they cease, God sees what they do.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: إِذْ يُوحِى رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ أَنِّى مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ۚ سَأُلْقِى فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلرُّعْبَ فَٱضْرِبُوا۟ فَوْقَ ٱلْأَعْنَاقِ وَٱضْرِبُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/8:12)
english: [Remember] when your Lord inspired to the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [them] upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip."
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 178
what_it_says: Angels are told to strengthen the believers and God will cast terror into the disbelievers; the command is to strike above the necks and at every fingertip (the Badr narrative).

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: وَأَعِدُّوا۟ لَهُم مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن قُوَّةٍ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِۦ عَدُوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ وَءَاخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُهُمْ ۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُوا۟ مِن شَىْءٍ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تُظْلَمُونَ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/8:60)
english: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allāh and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know [but] whom Allāh knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allāh will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 184
what_it_says: Believers are told to prepare all the power and steeds of war they can, to terrify the enemy of God and their enemy.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكْرَهُوا۟ شَيْـًٔا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تُحِبُّوا۟ شَيْـًٔا وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَّكُمْ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/2:216)
english: Battle has been enjoined upon you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allāh knows, while you know not.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 34
what_it_says: Fighting is prescribed for the believers though they dislike it, and a disliked thing may be good for them.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: وَقَـٰتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَـٰتِلُونَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُعْتَدِينَ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/2:190)
english: Fight in the way of Allāh those who fight against you but do not transgress. Indeed, Allāh does not like transgressors.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 29
what_it_says: Fight in God's way those who fight you, but do not transgress, for God does not love transgressors.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: وَٱقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ وَأَخْرِجُوهُم مِّنْ حَيْثُ أَخْرَجُوكُمْ ۚ وَٱلْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ ٱلْقَتْلِ ۚ وَلَا تُقَـٰتِلُوهُمْ عِندَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ حَتَّىٰ يُقَـٰتِلُوكُمْ فِيهِ ۖ فَإِن قَـٰتَلُوكُمْ فَٱقْتُلُوهُمْ ۗ كَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/2:191)
english: And kill them [in battle] wherever you overtake them and expel them from wherever they have expelled you, and fitnah is worse than killing. And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Ḥarām until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 30
what_it_says: Kill them wherever you find them and expel them from where they expelled you, since fitnah is worse than killing; fight them at the Sacred Mosque only if they fight you there first.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: وَقَـٰتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ ٱلدِّينُ لِلَّهِ ۖ فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوْا۟ فَلَا عُدْوَٰنَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/2:193)
english: Fight them until there is no [more] fitnah and [until] religion [i.e., worship] is [acknowledged to be] for Allāh. But if they cease, then there is to be no aggression [i.e., assault] except against the oppressors.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 30
what_it_says: Fight until there is no fitnah and religion is for God; if they cease, there is no aggression except against wrongdoers (double-edged: also read as a call to fight until shirk ends).

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلشَّهْرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ قِتَالٍ فِيهِ ۖ قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ ۖ وَصَدٌّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَكُفْرٌۢ بِهِۦ وَٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِۦ مِنْهُ أَكْبَرُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَٱلْفِتْنَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ ٱلْقَتْلِ ۗ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ يُقَـٰتِلُونَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَن دِينِكُمْ إِنِ ٱسْتَطَـٰعُوا۟ ۚ وَمَن يَرْتَدِدْ مِنكُمْ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَيَمُتْ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَـٰلُهُمْ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَـٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَـٰلِدُونَ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/2:217)
english: They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. Say, "Fighting therein is great [sin], but averting [people] from the way of Allāh and disbelief in Him and [preventing access to] al-Masjid al-Ḥarām and the expulsion of its people therefrom are greater [evil] in the sight of Allāh. And fitnah is greater than killing." And they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion [to disbelief] and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 34
what_it_says: Fighting in the sacred month is a great sin, but averting people from God's way, disbelief, and expulsion from the Sacred Mosque are worse, and fitnah is worse than killing; the disbelievers will keep fighting you if they can.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فَضَرْبَ ٱلرِّقَابِ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَثْخَنتُمُوهُمْ فَشُدُّوا۟ ٱلْوَثَاقَ فَإِمَّا مَنًّۢا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَآءً حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلْحَرْبُ أَوْزَارَهَا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ وَلَوْ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ لَٱنتَصَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَبْلُوَا۟ بَعْضَكُم بِبَعْضٍ ۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَلَن يُضِلَّ أَعْمَـٰلَهُمْ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/47:4)
english: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure [their] bonds, and either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allāh had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered armed struggle] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allāh - never will He waste their deeds.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 507
what_it_says: When you meet the disbelievers, strike the necks until you have inflicted slaughter, then bind captives; afterwards free them as favour or ransom them until the war lays down its burdens.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: قُل لِّلْمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ ٱلْأَعْرَابِ سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ أُو۟لِى بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ تُقَـٰتِلُونَهُمْ أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ ۖ فَإِن تُطِيعُوا۟ يُؤْتِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا ۖ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوْا۟ كَمَا تَوَلَّيْتُم مِّن قَبْلُ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/48:16)
english: Say to those who remained behind of the bedouins, "You will be called to [face] a people of great military might; you may fight them, or they will submit. So if you obey, Allāh will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment."
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 513
what_it_says: Those bedouins who stayed behind will be called to face a people of great might; you will fight them or they will submit.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَـٰتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا۟ ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/22:39)
english: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged. And indeed, Allāh is competent to give them victory.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 337
what_it_says: Permission to fight is given to those who are fought, because they have been wronged.

author: God (revelation)
date: revelation period c. 610-632 CE; Meccan/Medinan attribution varies by verse
arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَـٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَوَٰتٌ وَمَسَـٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
arabic_edition: quran.com API v4, field text_uthmani (api.quran.com/api/v4/verses/by_key/22:40)
english: [They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allāh." And were it not that Allāh checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allāh is much mentioned [i.e., praised]. And Allāh will surely support those who support Him [i.e., His cause]. Indeed, Allāh is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
translator: Saheeh International (quran.com translation id 20); footnote numerals stripped from the English. Hilali-Khan (id 203) also read in the raw file.
page: Madani Mushaf p. 337
what_it_says: Those expelled from their homes without right for saying 'Our Lord is Allah'; were God not checking people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques would be destroyed.

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: وهذه الآية الكريمة هي آية السيف التي قال فيها الضحاك بن مزاحم : إنها نسخت كل عهد بين النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وبين أحد من المشركين ، وكل عهد ، وكل مدة .
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/9:5; edition not named by the API)
english: This honorable Ayah (9:5) was called the Ayah of the Sword, about which Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said, "It abrogated every agreement of peace between the Prophet and any idolator, every treaty, and every term."
translator: Abridged Ibn Kathir (English) as served by quran.com (tafsir id 169); translator not named on API; brief identifies Darussalam abridged (Safiur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
page: quran.com section for 9:5; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir calls 9:5 the Ayah of the Sword and reports al-Dahhak saying it abrogated every peace agreement and treaty with idolaters.

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: قال علي بن أبي طالب : بعث النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بأربعة أسياف : سيف في المشركين من العرب قال الله : ( فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم [ وخذوهم ] )
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/9:5; edition not named by the API)
page: quran.com section for 9:5; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir records an 'Ali' report that the Prophet was sent with four swords (first against Arab idolaters); Ibn Kathir himself says he thinks the second sword is fighting the People of the Book, and the chain is given only as 'like this, abridged'.

author: Ibn Jarir al-Tabari (d. 310 AH / 923 CE)
arabic: =(وخذوهم) يقول: وأسروهم =(واحصروهم)، يقول: وامنعوهم من التصرف في بلاد الإسلام ودخول مكة =(واقعدوا لهم كل مرصد)، يقول: واقعدوا لهم بالطلب لقتلهم أو أسرهم
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 15 'Tafsir al-Tabari' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/15/by_ayah/9:5; edition not named)
page: quran.com text has no printed-page markers for this entry
what_it_says: Tabari glosses the verbs of 9:5 as: capture them, bar them from moving in Muslim lands and from entering Mecca, and lie in wait to kill or capture them.

author: Ibn Jarir al-Tabari (d. 310 AH / 923 CE)
arabic: وكان قتادة يقول: خلوا سبيل من أمركم الله أن تخلوا سبيله, فإنما الناس ثلاثة: رَهْط مسلم عليه الزكاة، ومشرك عليه الجزية، وصاحب حرب يأمن بتجارته في المسلمين إذا أعطى عُشُور ماله.
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 15 'Tafsir al-Tabari' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/15/by_ayah/9:5; edition not named)
page: quran.com text has no printed-page markers for this entry
what_it_says: Tabari reports Qatada's classification of people into three: a Muslim who owes zakat, an idolater who owes jizya, and a belligerent who may trade among Muslims if he pays a tithe on his goods.

author: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qurtubi (d. 671 AH / 1273 CE)
arabic: وفي هذا دليل على جواز اغتيالهم قبل الدعوة . ونصب ( كل ) على الظرف ، وهو اختيار الزجاج
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 90 'Al-Qurtubi' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/90/by_ayah/9:5; edition not named)
page: printed-page marker preceding passage: Qurtubi marker '[ص: 13]' (volume not stated)
what_it_says: Al-Qurtubi says the phrase 'lie in wait for them at every ambush' is evidence for the permissibility of assassinating them before the call (da'wa) is made.

author: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qurtubi (d. 671 AH / 1273 CE)
arabic: ثم اختلفوا ، فقال الحسين بن الفضل : نسخت هذه كل آية في القرآن فيها ذكر الإعراض والصبر على أذى الأعداء .
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 90 'Al-Qurtubi' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/90/by_ayah/9:5; edition not named)
page: printed-page marker preceding passage: Qurtubi marker '[ص: 13]' (volume not stated)
what_it_says: Al-Qurtubi reports al-Husayn b. al-Fadl saying 9:5 abrogated every Qur'anic verse mentioning turning away from and patience with the enemies' harm (note: the wording is narrower than 'every verse of pardon').

author: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qurtubi (d. 671 AH / 1273 CE)
arabic: وقال ابن زيد : الآيتان محكمتان . وهو الصحيح ؛ لأن المن والقتل والفداء لم يزل من حكم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيهم من أول حرب حاربهم ، وهو يوم بدر كما سبق .
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 90 'Al-Qurtubi' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/90/by_ayah/9:5; edition not named)
page: printed-page marker preceding passage: Qurtubi marker '[ص: 13]' (volume not stated)
what_it_says: Al-Qurtubi prefers Ibn Zayd's view that 9:5 and 47:4 are not abrogated, arguing that killing, ransom and release of captives were the Prophet's practice from the first battle, Badr.

author: al-Husayn b. Mas'ud al-Baghawi (d. 516 AH / 1122 CE)
arabic: والمرصد : الموضع الذي يرقب فيه العدو ، من رصدت الشيء أرصده : إذا ترقبته ، يريد : كونوا لهم رصدا لتأخذوهم من أي وجه توجهوا .
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 94 'Tafseer Al-Baghawi' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/94/by_ayah/9:5; edition not named)
page: quran.com section for 9:5; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Al-Baghawi glosses the ambush clause as 'be a watch for them so you seize them from whichever direction they turn', and also reports the view that they should wait on the Mecca road to stop them entering.

author: Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli (d. 864 AH) and Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (d. 911 AH)
arabic: ﴿فَإذا انْسَلَخَ﴾ خَرَجَ ﴿الأَشْهُر الحُرُم﴾ وهِيَ آخِر مُدَّة التَّأْجِيل ﴿فاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ فِي حِلّ أوْ حَرَم ﴿وخُذُوهُمْ﴾ بِالأَسْرِ ﴿واحْصُرُوهُمْ﴾ فِي القِلاع والحُصُون حَتّى يُضْطَرُّوا إلى القَتْل أوْ الإسْلام ﴿واقْعُدُوا لَهُمْ كُلّ مَرْصَد﴾ طَرِيق يَسْلُكُونَهُ ونُصِبَ كُلّ عَلى نَزْع الخافِض ﴿فَإنْ تابُوا﴾ مِن الكُفْر ﴿وأَقامُوا الصَّلاة وآتَوْا الزَّكاة فَخَلُّوا سَبِيلهمْ﴾ ولا تَتَعَرَّضُوا لَهُمْ ﴿إنّ اللَّه غَفُور رَحِيم﴾ لِمَن تابَ
arabic_edition: tafsir.app/jalalayn (Arabic, vocalized; site edition not named on the page)
english: Then when the sacred months have passed — that is at the end of the period of deferment — slay the idolaters wherever you find them be it during a lawful period or a sacred one and take them captive and confine them to castles and forts until they have no choice except being put to death or acceptance of Islam; and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush at every route that they use kulla ‘every’ is in the accusative because a preceding genitive-taking preposition has been removed. But if they repent of unbelief and establish prayer and pay the alms then leave their way free and do not interfere with them. God is Forgiving Merciful to those who repent.
translator: English: quranx.com 'Al-Jalalayn' page (translator not named on the page)
page: tafsir.app/jalalayn/9/5 (Arabic page; no printed page given on the site)
what_it_says: Al-Jalalayn explains 9:5's captives as confined in castles and forts 'until they have no choice except being put to death or acceptance of Islam'.

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: وقوله : ( حتى يعطوا الجزية ) أي : إن لم يسلموا ، ( عن يد ) أي : عن قهر لهم وغلبة ، ( وهم صاغرون ) أي : ذليلون حقيرون مهانون .
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/9:29; edition not named by the API)
english: (until they pay the Jizyah), if they do not choose to embrace Islam, (with willing submission), in defeat and subservience, (and feel themselves subdued.), disgraced, humiliated and belittled.
translator: Abridged Ibn Kathir (English) as served by quran.com (tafsir id 169); translator not named on API; brief identifies Darussalam abridged (Safiur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
page: quran.com section for 9:29; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir glosses 9:29's 'until they give the jizya' as applying if they do not embrace Islam, 'with submission' as defeat and subjugation, and 'humbled' as disgraced and humiliated.

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: ولهذا اشترط عليهم أمير المؤمنين عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - تلك الشروط المعروفة في إذلالهم وتصغيرهم وتحقيرهم
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/9:29; edition not named by the API)
english: This is why the Leader of the faithful `Umar bin Al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, demanded his well-known conditions be met by the Christians, these conditions that ensured their continued humiliation, degradation and disgrace.
translator: Abridged Ibn Kathir (English) as served by quran.com (tafsir id 169); translator not named on API; brief identifies Darussalam abridged (Safiur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
page: quran.com section for 9:29; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir presents the 'Pact of Umar' conditions (no new churches, muted bells, no displayed crosses, no riding saddles, no weapons, no beating Muslims) as humiliating terms, reporting them from 'Abd al-Rahman b. Ghanm via 'the scholars of hadith'; the chain is not checked in this work.

author: al-Husayn b. Mas'ud al-Baghawi (d. 516 AH / 1122 CE)
arabic: قال عكرمة : يعطون الجزية عن قيام ، والقابض جالس . وعن ابن عباس قال : تؤخذ منه ويوطأ عنقه .
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 94 'Tafseer Al-Baghawi' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/94/by_ayah/9:29; edition not named)
page: quran.com section for 9:29; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Al-Baghawi reports, citing Ibn Abbas and al-Kalbi, that the jizya payer is seized and his neck trampled, or slapped on the nape when paying; he also cites al-Kalbi that the first jizya taken by Muslims came from Qurayza and al-Nadir.

author: Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli (d. 864 AH) and Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (d. 911 AH)
arabic: ﴿حَتّى يُعْطُوا الجِزْيَة﴾ الخَراج المَضْرُوب عَلَيْهِمْ كُلّ عام ﴿عَنْ يَد﴾ حال أيْ مُنْقادِينَ أوْ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ لا يُوَكَّلُونَ بِها ﴿وهُمْ صاغِرُونَ﴾ أذِلّاء مُنْقادُونَ لِحُكْمِ الإسْلام
arabic_edition: tafsir.app/jalalayn (Arabic, vocalized; site edition not named on the page)
page: tafsir.app/jalalayn/9/29 (Arabic page; no printed page given on the site)
what_it_says: Al-Jalalayn defines jizya as the tax levied on them each year and 'humbled' as made submissive to the rule of Islam.

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: أمر الله تعالى المؤمنين أن يقاتلوا الكفار أولا فأولا الأقرب فالأقرب إلى حوزة الإسلام ؛ ولهذا بدأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بقتال المشركين في جزيرة العرب
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/9:123; edition not named by the API)
english: Allah commands the believers to fight the disbelievers, the closest in area to the Islamic state, then the farthest. This is why the Messenger of Allah ﷺ started fighting the idolators in the Arabian Peninsula.
translator: Abridged Ibn Kathir (English) as served by quran.com (tafsir id 169); translator not named on API; brief identifies Darussalam abridged (Safiur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
page: quran.com section for 9:123; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir reads 9:123 as an order to fight the nearest disbelievers first, which led from Arabia to fighting the Romans (Tabuk, year 9 AH).

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: وقوله : ( ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين ) أي : قاتلوا في سبيل الله ولا تعتدوا في ذلك ويدخل في ذلك ارتكاب المناهي كما قاله الحسن البصري من المثلة ، والغلول ، وقتل النساء والصبيان والشيوخ الذين لا رأي لهم ولا قتال فيهم ، والرهبان وأصحاب الصوامع ، وتحريق الأشجار وقتل الحيوان لغير مصلحة
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/2:190; edition not named by the API)
english: Al-Hasan Al-Basri stated that transgression (indicated by the Ayah), "includes mutilating the dead, theft (from the captured goods), killing women, children and old people who do not participate in warfare, killing priests and residents of houses of worship, burning down trees and killing animals without real benefit."
translator: Abridged Ibn Kathir (English) as served by quran.com (tafsir id 169); translator not named on API; brief identifies Darussalam abridged (Safiur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
page: quran.com section for 2:190; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir lists the prohibited acts under 'do not transgress' (2:190): mutilation, theft from booty, killing of women, children, non-combatant old men, monks, and burning trees, reporting this from al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Abbas and Umar b. Abd al-Aziz.

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: وفي هذا نظر ; لأن قوله : ( الذين يقاتلونكم ) إنما هو تهييج وإغراء بالأعداء الذين همتهم قتال الإسلام وأهله
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/2:190; edition not named by the API)
english: However, this statement is not plausible, because Allah's statement: (...those who fight you) applies only to fighting the enemies who are engaged in fighting Islam and its people.
translator: Abridged Ibn Kathir (English) as served by quran.com (tafsir id 169); translator not named on API; brief identifies Darussalam abridged (Safiur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
page: quran.com section for 2:190; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir rejects the view that 2:190 was abrogated, reading 'those who fight you' as the enemies who are actively fighting Islam and its people.

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/2:190; edition not named by the API)
english: In this Hadith, Allah's Messenger ﷺ mentions fighting the people of Makkah when he conquered it by force, leading to some deaths among the polytheists in the area of the Khandamah.
translator: Abridged Ibn Kathir (English) as served by quran.com (tafsir id 169); translator not named on API; brief identifies Darussalam abridged (Safiur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
page: quran.com section for 2:190; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith on the sanctity of Makkah in which the Prophet fought the people of Makkah when he conquered it by force, which he uses to explain the 'unless they fight you there' exception to the Sacred Mosque rule.

author: Ibn Jarir al-Tabari (d. 310 AH / 923 CE)
arabic: يقول تعالى ذكره لنبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم: وقاتلوا المشركين الذين يقاتلونكم حتى لا تكون فتنة = يعني: حتى لا يكون شركٌ بالله، وحتى لا يُعبد دونه أحدٌ،
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 15 'Tafsir al-Tabari' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/15/by_ayah/2:193; edition not named)
page: no marker before passage; first following printed-page marker: Tabari marker '3-571' (vol-page)
what_it_says: Tabari glosses 2:193 as 'fight the polytheists who fight you until there is no shirk', and reports Qatada, Mujahid and Ibn Abbas that fitnah means shirk.

author: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qurtubi (d. 671 AH / 1273 CE)
arabic: وهو أمر بقتال مطلق لا بشرط أن يبدأ الكفار . دليل ذلك قوله تعالى : " ويكون الدين لله " ، وقال عليه السلام : أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله ، فدلت الآية والحديث على أن سبب القتال هو الكفر
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 90 'Al-Qurtubi' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/90/by_ayah/2:193; edition not named)
page: no marker before passage; first following printed-page marker: Qurtubi marker '[ص: 330]' (volume not stated)
what_it_says: Al-Qurtubi says 2:193 is an unconditional command to fight every polytheist, not conditional on their attacking first, and that the cause of fighting is disbelief.

author: al-Husayn b. Mas'ud al-Baghawi (d. 516 AH / 1122 CE)
arabic: ثم أمره بقتال المشركين كافة قاتلوا أو لم يقاتلوا بقوله ( فاقتلوا المشركين ) فصارت هذه الآية منسوخة بها
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 94 'Tafseer Al-Baghawi' (api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/94/by_ayah/2:190; edition not named)
page: quran.com section for 2:190; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Al-Baghawi reports the view that 2:190 was abrogated by 'kill the polytheists', so that the Prophet was commanded to fight the polytheists 'whether they fight or not'; he also gives the opposite view that 2:190 is muhkam and 'do not transgress' means not killing women, children, the old and monks.

author: Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli (d. 864 AH) and Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (d. 911 AH)
arabic: ﴿وقاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيل اللَّه﴾ أيْ لِإعْلاءِ دِينه ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ﴾ الكُفّار ﴿ولا تَعْتَدُوا﴾ عَلَيْهِمْ بِالِابْتِداءِ بِالقِتالِ ﴿إنّ اللَّه لا يُحِبّ المُعْتَدِينَ﴾ المُتَجاوِزِينَ ما حَدّ لَهُمْ وهَذا مَنسُوخ بِآيَةِ بَراءَة أوْ بِقَوْلِهِ:
arabic_edition: tafsir.app/jalalayn (Arabic, vocalized; site edition not named on the page)
page: tafsir.app/jalalayn/2/190 (Arabic page; no printed page given on the site)

author: Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli (d. 864 AH) and Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (d. 911 AH)
arabic: ﴿وأَخْرِجُوهُمْ مِن حَيْثُ أخْرَجُوكُمْ﴾ أيْ مِن مَكَّة وقَدْ فَعَلَ بِهِمْ ذَلِكَ عام الفَتْح ﴿والفِتْنَة﴾ الشِّرْك مِنهُمْ ﴿أشَدّ﴾ أعْظَم ﴿مِن القَتْل﴾

what_it_says: Al-Jalalayn says the 'expel them from where they expelled you' clause was carried out against the Meccans in the year of the Conquest, and that fitnah means their shirk.

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: ثم أمر تعالى بقتال الكفار : ( حتى لا تكون فتنة ) أي : شرك . قاله ابن عباس ، وأبو العالية ، ومجاهد ، والحسن ، وقتادة ، والربيع ، ومقاتل بن حيان ، والسدي ، وزيد بن أسلم .

work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic; English abridged for EN)
author: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH / 1373 CE)
arabic: قال : قاتلنا حتى لم تكن فتنة وكان الدين لله ، وأنتم تريدون أن تقاتلوا حتى تكون فتنة ويكون الدين لغير الله .
arabic_edition: quran.com tafsir id 14 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' (API api.quran.com/api/v4/tafsirs/14/by_ayah/2:193; edition not named by the API)
english: He said, "We did fight until there was no more Fitnah and the religion became for Allah Alone. You want to fight until there is Fitnah and the religion becomes for other than Allah!"
translator: Abridged Ibn Kathir (English) as served by quran.com (tafsir id 169); translator not named on API; brief identifies Darussalam abridged (Safiur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
page: quran.com section for 2:193; no printed page in the source
what_it_says: Ibn Kathir reports Ibn Umar's answer to rebels who quoted 2:193: the Muslims fought until fitnah ended, and the rebels were now asking for fitnah; Ibn Kathir attributes the exchange to al-Bukhari (in-book number not verified).
